claims.hypothesis: The outer dust ring observed by ALMA around 48 au coincides with a volatile condensation line.

limitations_admitted.value: The intermediate disc is spatially unresolved by current interferometry, leaving a large degeneracy in its outer extent (up to 5-7 au).

evidence.quote: However, the dimensions of this intermediate disc are not constrained by interferometry or other spatially resolved methods. This means that there exists a large set of acceptable models of this region, extending up to 5 – 7 au.

referee_caveats_inferred: Shellspec imposes parametric power-law temperature profiles and vertical isothermality rather than solving self-consistent Monte Carlo dust thermal radiative equilibrium, which likely drives the high 50-60 K mid-plane temperature needed to fit the far-IR SED.

There is a factor of 10 discrepancy between the accretion rate in the text/Conclusions (6.1e-8 M_sun/yr) and the statement that it is 'surprisingly similar' to Bouvier et al. 2020a (quoted in the Introduction as 6.5e-9 M_sun/yr), suggesting a possible typo in the exponent.
Fitting the inner, intermediate, and outer regions separately rather than globally may miss radiative shadowing effects from the misaligned inner disc onto the outer ring.

data_public_as_stated.value: Public archival data from the ALMA Science Archive, ESO Science Archive Facility (with DOIs provided), Gaia, and VizieR.

evidence.quote: To constrain the physical properties of the accretion region around the star, all available H$\alpha$ datasets from the ESO Archive were utilized.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data sets: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00532.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.01111.S.

Based on data obtained from the ESO Science Archive Facility with DOI(s): <https://doi.eso.org/10.18727/archive/21>, <https://doi.eso.org/10.18727/archive/50>, <https://doi.eso.org/10.18727/archive/71>.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-200 GB (dominated by high-resolution ALMA Band 6 and Band 7 archival visibility datasets)
reproducibility.score_reason: All raw observational data (ALMA, VLT, VLTI, VizieR SED) and the core modelling codes (Shellspec/Pyshellspec, emcee) are public, and best-fit model parameters are tabulated. However, the ALMA visibility extraction/averaging steps, exact SED flux table, assumed source distance, and trial-and-error parameter scan grids are not fully specified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All ALMA and ESO/VLTI datasets are publicly available in archives, and the analytic MCMC visibility fitting (step 2) as well as the parametric radiative transfer fits produce concrete numerical values for disc inclinations, ring radii, and accretion rates.

methods_papers.why: Describes the Pyshellspec tool used to compute synthetic interferometric, spectroscopic, and photometric observables and chi^2.
Describes the underlying Shellspec 3D long-characteristics radiative-transfer code.
Provides the analytic visibility models (ellipse/ring with star and halo) used to fit VLTI and ALMA visibilities.
MCMC sampler used for fitting the analytic visibility models.

companion_papers.why: Published and analysed the high-resolution ALMA Band 7 (2019.1.00532.S) and Band 6 observations of DoAr 44 reused here.
ODISEA survey paper that published the high-resolution ALMA Band 6 dataset (2018.1.00028.S) of DoAr 44.
Published the VLTI/GRAVITY data and optical spectroscopy/photometry of DoAr 44 reused and compared in this work.
